I1.quote: Gravimetric H2 (BIP+, Air Products) uptake isotherms up to 100 bar were measured at −196 °C on a Hiden XEMIS gravimetric sorption analyser.

I2.quote: After the carbonization step, the carbon microspheres (CS) are mainly composed by C, i.e. >90 wt%, with a very low O content.
I2.location: main, p. 3, Section 3.1; Table 2 (p. 4) gives C 93.54 wt% for CS; Table S1 (SI, p. 1) gives C 93.92-94.38 wt% for the activated samples whose H2 uptake is measured

I3.quote: CS-835-78 has an uptake of 8.51 wt% at 100 bar and −196 °C
I3.location: main, p. 6, Section 3.2; also Table 3 (p. 5), column 'H2 storage (wt%) Measured, −196 °C, 100 bar', and Fig. 3 (p. 6), axes H2 uptake (wt%) vs P (bar), caption 'measured at −196 °C, up to 100 bar'

I4.location: main, p. 5, Table 3, row CS-885-82; the 3299 is under column ABET (m2 g−1) and the 9.19 under H2 storage (wt%), Measured, −196 °C, 100 bar. ABET is a BET area from N2 at −196 °C (Section 2.2, p. 2-3), reported for every activated sample whose H2 uptake is measured

I5.quote: Highly porous carbon microspheres have been obtained by a sustainable and facile approach that combines a microwave-assisted sol-gel process with a physical activation process.

notes: Original experimental paper (gravimetric Hiden XEMIS isotherms at -196 C up to 100 bar on CO2-activated carbon microspheres, uptake up to 9.19 wt%, ABET up to 3299 m2/g). is_retracted false in record.json; no retraction notice found in main text or SI. Only 'previously reported' wording concerns the synthesis procedure (ref. 16), not the H2 uptake values, so duplicate_data does not apply. The -123 C values in Table 3 are Toth-method predictions (theoretical) and are not relied on; the measured -196 C isotherms suffice. Uptake is stated to be on a total-adsorption basis (derived from net/excess isotherms), which does not affect eligibility.
